title: Rank-one compactness comparison surjective
statement: For any ring S in universe w, with the indicated derived category and coproducts, and any family E indexed by I : Type (max w vH), the canonical additive map from the direct sum of Hom(P,E i) to Hom(P,coproduct E) is surjective, where P is the degree-zero single complex on ModuleCat.of S (ULift.{vH} S).

proof.text: The lifted regular module is free and projective. Its degree-zero single complex has projective terms and is bounded above, so Mathlib CochainComplex.isKProjective_of_projective makes it K-projective. CochainComplex.IsKProjective.Qh_map_bijective and the full homotopy quotient show that every derived map from it to Q(L) lifts to a chain map. This is proved as rankOne_kProjective and rankOne_map_surjective in the delivered module.

For a family K of complexes, form the coproduct projections p_i, equal to the identity on summand i and zero on every other summand. Evaluation in degree zero preserves this coproduct. Its colimit cocone is isomorphic to the concrete module direct sum (ModuleCat.coproductCoconeIsColimit). For a chain map f from the rank-one single complex, evaluate f on the lifted unit and express the result as v in that direct sum. Direct-sum induction shows that applying p_i recovers v_i. Hence f is the sum, over the finite support of v, of (f followed by p_i) followed by the ith coprojection: equality in degree zero follows from DirectSum.sum_support_of and linearity, and equality of chain maps follows from HomologicalComplex.from_single_hom_ext. This proves rankOne_chain_finite_sum, including empty families and the zero ring.

For each derived object E_i take the complex Q.objPreimage(E_i), with its canonical isomorphism Q(K_i) to E_i. Apply derivedModuleDirectSums to identify Q of the termwise coproduct with the coproduct of the Q(K_i), then transport through these isomorphisms. Lift the given morphism to a chain map by step 1, and write that map as the finite sum from step 2. Put the localized coordinate maps, transported to E_i, in the algebraic direct sum of Hom groups. Additivity of Q and the defining equations for the coproduct isomorphisms show that the comparison sends this element to the original morphism.

proof_origin.place: first paragraph: rank-one compactness assertion; explicit chain-map finite-support calculation using Mathlib K-projective localization

Morphisms from a free module concentrated in degree zero to an arbitrary derived object are cohomology classes

12 hits including homology functors and DerivedCategory.isIso_iff; no rank-one detection or compactness theorem.
K-projectivity and localization bijectivity APIs exist; no complete match. Local rg of both library roots found no duplicate of either new statement.

mathlib_searches.query: In a preadditive category with coproducts the direct sum of Hom groups injects into Hom to the coproduct
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: biproduct and module coproduct APIs, no matching theorem. The projection argument proves injectivity directly.
toAddMonoid_injective concerns injectivity in the family of additive maps, not the induced map on elements; no complete match.
No public duplicate. CompactHomHocolim has a private coordinate calculation, which additionally assumes compactness; injectivity is proved here without that assumption.

lean.statement:
theorem derivedModule_rankOne_comparison_surjective
    {S : Type w} [Ring S]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{max w vH} (ModuleCat.{max w vH} S)]
    [HasCoproducts.{max w vH} (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max w vH} S))]
    (I : Type (max w vH))
    (E : I → DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max w vH} S)) :
    let _ := Classical.decEq I
    let P := (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max w vH} S) 0).obj
      (ModuleCat.of S (ULift.{vH} S))
    Function.Surjective
      (DirectSum.toAddMonoid (fun i : I => Preadditive.rightComp P (Sigma.ι E i)) :
        (⨁ i : I, (P ⟶ E i)) →+ (P ⟶ ∐ E))
